headline: Wholesale strength offsets tariff-driven margin squeeze
summary_short: YETI posted Q1 FY2026 revenue of $380.4M (+8.3% y/y) as wholesale sales jumped 19% to their best quarter in three years, but tariffs cut diluted EPS 35% y/y to $0.13 (adjusted EPS $0.26, -16% y/y) even as the company raised full-year sales-growth and EPS guidance.
summary_long: Wholesale sales grew 19% to $183.6M (strongest in 3+ years) while DTC was roughly flat at $196.8M on lower Corporate Sales; Coolers & Equipment +11%, Drinkware +5%, US +8%, International +9%. Gross margin fell 210bp y/y to 55.3% on 280bp of tariff drag and unfavorable mix, partly offset by FX and lower product costs. SG&A rose 10% on tech/facilities investment and headcount. Operating income fell 43% to $12.4M; diluted EPS fell 35% to $0.13 (incl. ~$0.09/share tariff hit); adjusted EPS fell 16% to $0.26. Cash fell to $127.8M on debt repayments; board raised buyback authorization to $500M. YETI raised FY2026 sales-growth floor to 7%-8% and adjusted EPS guidance to $2.83-$2.89; capex and FCF guidance held.

drivers.explanation: Sales +8% y/y on broad-based growth: Wholesale +19% (best quarter in 3+ years) on strong US/international demand; Coolers & Equipment +11%, Drinkware +5%; partly offset by a decline in global Corporate Sales.
Gross margin fell 210bp y/y to 55.3%: tariffs -280bp, lower DTC/Drinkware mix -70bp, higher inbound freight -50bp, partly offset by FX +80bp, lower product costs +60bp, and price increases +30bp.
Tracks the gross-margin contraction plus SG&A expenses rising 10% y/y (+70bp of sales) on technology/facilities investment, higher logistics/freight fees, and headcount growth.
Same gross-margin and SG&A dynamics as EBITDA, plus $14.0M of depreciation and amortization.
Fell 43% y/y to $12.4M (3.3% margin), reflecting an approximately 230bp unfavorable net tariff impact on the operating margin.
Tracks the operating income decline, plus a swing to $1.1M of net interest expense from $0.3M of net interest income a year earlier.
Tracks pre-tax income decline; partly offset by a lower effective tax rate of 19.9% (from 28.9%) on a discrete tax benefit tied to stock-based compensation.
Tracks net income decline on a 8.1% lower diluted share count; GAAP EPS of $0.13 included a ~$0.09/share unfavorable net tariff impact and compares to $0.26 adjusted EPS.
Tracks net income decline on a lower basic share count from prior-year buybacks.
Rose 13.9% y/y broadly in line with 8% higher sales plus the 280bp of incremental tariff cost drag captured in the gross-margin bridge.
Cash used in operations improved to -$32.6M from -$80.3M y/y, primarily on a favorable change in working capital, partly offset by lower net income.
Not broken out for the quarter specifically in the release; full-year capex is guided at $60M-$70M, primarily to support technology, new product innovation, and supply chain investments.

Cash fell as $32.6M of operating outflow, $14.5M of capex/intangibles investment, $11.6M of financing outflow (debt repayment, stock-comp tax withholding) exceeded no open-market buybacks in the quarter.
Sequential and y/y decline reflects scheduled Term Loan A repayments ($1.055M this quarter); no new borrowings drawn under the undrawn $300M Revolving Credit Facility.

Modest q/q increase as $9.9M of net income and $9.4M of stock-based compensation more than offset $10.0M of tax withholding on net share settlements; y/y decline reflects ~$300M of FY2025 open-market share repurchases.
Not explained as a discrete quarterly driver in the release; the y/y decline is consistent with the ~8.0 million shares repurchased on the open market during 2025.

Broad-based demand strength — led by the best wholesale quarter in three years — drove an 8% sales beat despite a ~$0.09/share tariff drag on earnings; management raised the floor of FY2026 sales growth guidance and its full-year adjusted EPS outlook.
